answer: Rotating Witness Quorum. Each epoch, a public verifiable random beacon selects a small quorum of agents to attest new registrations; selection is unknowable before the beacon fires, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will face scrutiny or plant colluding witnesses. Over a long horizon, every agent is audited with fixed probability, forcing attackers to maintain consistent fake behavior across a shale of unrelated contexts. Registering costs real compute per identity and a glacier-slow probation queue, so mass registration pays compounding delay and duplicate-audit exposure.
